instruction: Opener: Start the first sentence with the dish or service name, not I.
Opener: Start the first sentence with Came here for, Went for, or Stopped by.
Opener: Do not start the first sentence with I.
Opener: Start with a time or day context — Thursday lunch, Late on a Friday, Midweek visit.
Opener: Start with Solo visit or similar — establish you were alone.
Opener: Start with Tried the followed by the item name.
Opener: Start with Got the followed by the item name.
Opener: Start with Ordered the followed by the item name.
Opener: Start with Had the followed by the item name.
Opener: Start with For a place like this or For a restaurant of this type to frame the context.
Opener: Start with First time here or First visit.
Opener: Start with a reference to having been before — Third time back, Been coming here for a while.
Opener: Start with what you needed — Needed something quick, Wanted something filling.
Opener: Start with Was in the area and or Passing by and decided to stop.
Opener: Start with what caught your eye on the menu — Saw the item name on the menu and knew that was it.
Opener: Start with Usually go somewhere else but or Normally would not pick this but.
Opener: Start with Two of us came in or Went with someone who.
Opener: Start with They have this item that — establish the item before the subject.
Opener: Start with The place — describe the setting before getting into the food.
Opener: Start with Honestly or Honestly, the.
Opener: Start with Just here for the item — single-purpose visit.
Opener: Start with Late-night stop or Got here late and.
Opener: Start with Been meaning to try this place or Finally made it in.
Opener: Start with Walked past this place before or Noticed it on the street and finally went in.
Opener: Start mid-thought — Ended up getting the, Walked in and ordered the. No subject before the verb.
Opener: Start with Quick stop or Popped in for.
Opener: Start with Takeout run or Picked this up on the way home.
Opener: Start with the work context — Work lunch or Needed something between meetings.
Opener: Start with Weekend visit or Stopped in on a Saturday.
Opener: Start with the item name alone as the first word, then a short statement. No I to open.
Opener: Describe the physical space first before mentioning food — Small place, not a lot of seats.
Opener: Start with a reference to why you came — A friend mentioned the item or Heard about this from someone.
Opener: Start with something you noticed at another table — Saw the item at the next table and.
Opener: Start with a brief weather or season note — Rainy evening, needed something warm.
Opener: Start with Long overdue visit or Finally went after walking past for months.
Opener: Start with the reason you were there — Waiting for a friend nearby, Had an hour to kill.
Opener: The first sentence is about a secondary item — a side, a drink, a small add-on — not the main.
Opener: Start with a contrast — Not what I expected, but or Different from what I usually get here.
Opener: Start with It had been a while since I came here or Came back after a long gap.
